open_items.detail:

open_items.item: CLOSED - CRITICAL - the device-grant OAuth flow is unreachable on any real server (GAP-1 on the server side)
open_items.detail:
apps/server config/{config,dev,prod,runtime}.exs never set ':keepling, :device_grants'. The key is supplied ONLY by test setup (apps/server/test/keepling_web/device_grant_controller_test.exs:15, sync_controller_test.exs:14, accounts/device_grant_test.exs:22), which puts issuer/origin/server_instance/redirect_uris via Application.put_env. Consequence on a running server: allowed_redirect?/2 (device_grant.ex:714) reads Application.get_env(:keepling, :device_grants, [])[:redirect_uris], gets %{}, and returns false for every redirect_uri -- so /oauth/authorize always answers 400 invalid_authorization_request; and namespace_config/0, called by issue/3 and exchange/2, returns {:error, :device_grant_configuration_missing}. Three of the five locked namespace-tuple fields (issuer, origin, server_instance) come from this block. Net: no device grant can be issued or exchanged outside the test suite. Same signature as GAP-1 -- a complete, well-tested subsystem that is unreachable in production because its only configuration lives in test setup. OWNED BY 03-14 Task 1, which adds real runtime configuration plus fail-fast pre-supervision validation so an unconfigured server refuses to boot instead of failing later at /oauth/authorize. CLOSED 2026-09-02 by 03-14 Task 1: runtime.exs supplies :device_grants in every environment and Keepling.Application.validate_device_grants!/1 refuses to boot without it. Note infra/compose/compose.yml also required updating or compose boot would have broken.

CLOSED 2026-09-03 (reconciliation): closed by 03-14 (fc9823d, 4fc703e). :keepling, :device_grants now comes from real runtime configuration in every environment (apps/server/config/runtime.exs:152) and Keepling.Application.validate_device_grants!/1 refuses to boot an unconfigured server instead of answering a silent 400.

open_items.item: CLOSED - Quick Entry now returns focus to the prior application
open_items.detail: Found by 03-15 row A9 and documented in 03-15-SUMMARY.md:206, but NOT recorded in HANDOFF.json by the executor -- added here 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator. QuickEntryWindowController calls an optional `foregroundApp` port on open and hide, but NO implementation of that port exists anywhere in the repository and none is passed in main/index.ts#bootstrap(). Prior-app focus return is therefore unreachable in the shipped app. MEASURED, not inferred: with TextEdit focused, submitting a Quick Entry capture leaves Keepling frontmost. Differs from O-1/O-11/O-12/O-15 in that the adapter was never written at all, so closing it is new implementation work (a ForegroundAppPort adapter plus bootstrap wiring) and it carries a real UX decision: what should happen when Quick Entry is invoked from Keepling own window. Disclosed rather than half-fixed. Row A9 fails honestly against it, so the phase gate is RED until it is closed. CLOSED 2026-09-03 by 03-16 (e2bc5ea, 06ac82d, 14a2f4b). `ElectronForegroundApp` in apps/desktop/main/windows/foreground-app.ts is constructed in the production bootstrap() and passed as QuickEntryWindowController's `foregroundApp`. Mechanism: capture records ONLY whether Keepling itself was frontmost; restore calls app.hide(), and macOS hands activation back to the previously active application with the caret untouched -- no TCC Automation prompt, no native module. The UX decision O-21 flagged was resolved as: invoked from Keepling's own window, do NOT hide -- show and focus the main window instead (proven by unit test, since row A9 cannot measure it). The option is now REQUIRED on QuickEntryWindowOptions, so this defect class cannot recur silently. MEASURED: row A9 PASS cases=6 against application_digest=ffcb4a92459956e21708b415f4b4b8b0babde91452ee308a5e633e766d346c59, and the full lane is rows=15 failed=0 cases=92 with LANE_EVIDENCE recorded=true and SETTINGS restore=VERIFIED. open_items.item: Focus return is implemented by hiding the WHOLE application, which also hides Keepling's main window
open_items.detail: Consequence of the mechanism chosen to close O-21, recorded because row A9 does not measure it and a dogfooder will notice it. macOS only hands activation back to the previous application when an application hides ITSELF, so restoring focus necessarily hides Keepling's main window too: capture from TextEdit with a Keepling window visible on the same space, and after the capture commits that window is gone (hidden, not closed) rather than merely behind TextEdit. Every alternative examined needs something we refuse to ship: activating another application by bundle identifier needs its identity, which needs an AppleScript/Automation TCC prompt (prohibited by 03-16) or a native NSRunningApplication module. The next capture un-hides the app again, so nothing is stranded. DECIDE at dogfood: accept it, or ship a native helper. Do NOT 'fix' it by skipping app.hide(), which silently reintroduces O-21 -- row A9 would go red, correctly.

open_items.item: CLOSED - the macOS lane no longer contains sleep-then-read-once patterns
open_items.detail: CLOSED - every sleep-then-read-once site in the lane now settles on the condition it asserts. Fixed by 03-18 (509e323), which converted A1 (enabled state, sync status), A2 (row announcements, roving focus, selection), A3 (both dialogs and the conflict heading), A5 (detail mount, Complete/Reopen, final focus), A6 (both dialog focus reads), A8 (settings pane, arbitration), A9 (caret before/after, frontmost return), A11 (selection, disabled state), A14 (the live re-theme now settles on legibility, not merely on the background having changed) and A15 (layout reflow after resize). A6's ad-hoc polling loop was folded into settledFocus, so the file has exactly two waiting mechanisms: settledFocus(handle, {until}) for AX focus and waitFor for everything else. No assertion was weakened; waitFor gained onTimeout:'return' so a deadline hands the last observation to the caller's own check instead of aborting the row with only a timeout. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the rule as previously stated here: the settle predicate must NOT be 'strictly weaker than the assertion' / 'wait for focus to stop moving'. Quiescence settles on the failure state, because an absent focus and a pending dead key are both stable indefinitely. The correct rule, now written into waitFor's own documentation in the lane, is: poll for the CONDITION YOU ARE ABOUT TO ASSERT, to a bounded deadline, and report the last observation if it never holds. That does not make a row vacuous -- a condition that never holds still fails. MEASURED after the fix: ten consecutive `--all` runs, 150/150 row executions passed, 92 cases each, all ten reporting SETTINGS restore=VERIFIED; runs 4 and 7 under full CPU load (18 spinners on 18 cores) took 222s and 208s against an idle 168-171s and still passed. See 03-18-SUMMARY.md.

open_items.item: CLOSED - vacuous negation assertions swept in vitest (03-18) and in the Playwright e2e/packaged suites (03-19)
open_items.detail:
Found by 03-18 while converting row A8. Both A8 phases asserted 'Keepling does not report the Quick Entry accelerator as unavailable' (!/Quick Entry shortcut isn.t available/.test(settingsText)) against a settings pane read once after a fixed sleep(1800). An empty or half-rendered pane satisfies that negation, so a slow Settings window would have produced a PASS rather than a failure -- a false pass, not a flake. Fixed in 509e323 by waiting for the pane to have STATED a position (either 'Current shortcut' or the unavailable message) and failing the row loudly if it never does; that wait deliberately does NOT use onTimeout:'return', because returning would restore the vacuous read. Only A8 was found to have this shape in the macOS lane, but the class is not lane-specific: any assertion of the form 'the text does NOT contain X' is vacuously true against an unrendered read. The Playwright E2E suites and the packaged lane have not been swept for it.

CLOSED 2026-09-03 by 03-19, which swept test/e2e/** and test/packaged/**. All 24 negation sites were enumerated with a verdict each (full table in 03-19-SUMMARY.md). Six were vacuous and were GUARDED with a positive read, none weakened or deleted: accessibility.spec.ts:83 and :93 (a negated Playwright locator matcher PASSES against a locator resolving to nothing, so a row that never rendered reported a pass -- now guarded with toBeVisible()); :260 (both colour readings now asserted to be real resolved colours before being compared); :274 (not.toBe('') admits any non-colour value); :290 (the strongest -- the evaluate returns null when there is no button to measure, and null !== '0s' passed, so a window that rendered no controls 'proved' motion was enabled); packaged/security.spec.ts:159 (not.toBe('granted') passed for undefined; now asserts the permission was actually DENIED). The other eighteen were already guarded by an adjacent positive assertion or by a read that throws, and were left untouched.

open_items.item: Ten green runs BOUND the lane's flake rate; they do not prove it is zero
open_items.detail: Recorded so the number is not overclaimed later. 0 failures in 10 full runs (150 row executions) bounds the per-RUN failure rate below roughly 26-30% and the per-ROW rate below roughly 2%, at 95% confidence (rule of three). The historical rates it replaces were much larger -- A4 failed 3 in 6, A7 roughly 1 in 8 -- so the improvement is real and measured, but a residual rate of a few percent per row would not have been detected by this experiment. If a row flakes again, the response is to fix the race in that row, never to re-record until a run happens to pass. Related reading trap in the same area: the recorded evidence's `source_revision` field is the git HEAD at which the PACKAGE was built (tooling/package-desktop.mjs:158), not the revision of the lane that produced the evidence -- it read 55b9398 for evidence recorded at 509e323. That is not a defect (the artifact digest and the lane-source digest are what the gate actually binds to, and the lane-source binding was verified live by 03-18: appending one comment to the lane made the gate refuse the evidence with 'the lane's own source changed since that evidence was recorded'), but the field looks stale to a human reading the line and should not be used to judge freshness.

open_items.item: CLOSED - the desktop 'offline' presentation state is real, constructed in production, and proven to reach a user
open_items.detail:
MAC-04 requires the user to inspect offline, syncing, conflict, authentication-expired and unrecoverable states. Mapped onto the real vocabulary in apps/desktop/main/application/presentation.ts these are offline / updating / conflict / authentication_required / store_unavailable. Four are genuinely published: updating at DesktopApplication.ts:446,449; authentication_required at main/index.ts:462; store_unavailable at DesktopApplication.ts:250,377; and per-task conflict is surfaced through the workspace conflict region in packages/web-ui (21 refs, covered by state-matrix.test.tsx). `{ kind: 'offline' }` is DECLARED in the DesktopPresentationInput union (presentation.ts:35), has authored copy ('Offline -- showing tasks saved on this Mac'), and is unit-tested at test/application/recovery-presentation.test.ts:23 -- but grep across apps/ packages/ tooling/ finds NO production construction anywhere. The sync pass settles only into healthy / local_saved / retryable_failure (DesktopApplication.ts:483,486). A user who unplugs the network therefore never sees the offline state; they see retryable_failure copy instead. This is the same shape as O-9/O-11/O-12/O-15/O-16/O-21: complete, tested, unreachable. It was NOT caught by the mechanical GAP-1 sweep, which looks for exported SYMBOLS referenced only by tests; this is a union VARIANT never constructed, which that sweep cannot see. Generalise the detector to state variants before trusting it as a clean bill of health.

CLOSED 2026-09-03 by 03-19. The discriminator lives in the transport, the only layer that knows whether bytes came back: KeeplingSyncAdapter#json wraps the fetch call alone and rethrows a tagged SyncUnreachableError (main/application/sync-reachability.ts), and runSyncPass() reads the tag -- it never sniffs message text. A server that ANSWERED badly (500, malformed body, bounded-page violation) still lands on retryable_failure. An app with no server configured makes no request at all and settles offline with a null contact, because healthy would read as 'everything is synchronized' and local_saved promises a sync nothing is arranged to perform. lastSuccessfulContact has a durable source: NodeSqliteLocalStore.recordSuccessfulContact writes the instant the server answered into namespace_metadata, it is routed through the store-worker protocol and forwarded by WorkerLocalStore, and syncState() reads it back across relaunches; it is null when the server has never answered. Proof is shipped-entry-point, not fixture: test/e2e/gap-closure.spec.ts launches the real dist/main/index.cjs with the real KeeplingSyncAdapter (KEEPLING_TEST_SYNC_MODE deliberately unset) against a closed loopback port, a real 500 server, and no server at all, and reads the row off the rendered window. Gate: lanes=9 failed=0. NOTE the generalisation in this item is NOT closed and is carried forward as O-33: the mechanical GAP-1 sweep still cannot see a union VARIANT that is never constructed.

open_items.item: NO renderer surface rendered ANY presentation copy -- MAC-04's rows were published to a renderer that displayed none of them. Fixed for the desktop MAIN window only.
open_items.detail: Found by 03-19 while proving O-30. DesktopApplication has published a closed, main-owned presentation row for every synchronization and recovery state since 03-05, and the preload bridge has delivered it with a sequence contract since 03-08 -- but nothing ever RENDERED summary.copy. renderer/desktopClientFacade.ts subscribed to the presentation channel only to trigger a snapshot refetch, and grep for the authored copy strings across packages/web-ui, apps/desktop/renderer and apps/desktop/preload found no render site at all. So EVERY one of MAC-04's rows -- not just offline -- was unreachable to a person, and the e2e RED for O-30 failed identically for all three cases with 'locator(#sync-status-row) element(s) not found'. This is the same class as O-9/O-11/O-12/O-15/O-16/O-21/O-30: complete, tested, unreachable. PARTIALLY CLOSED: 03-19 added apps/desktop/renderer/SyncStatusRow.tsx and wired it into DesktopShell, so the MAIN window now renders main's copy verbatim (null copy renders nothing, so healthy and the anti-flicker grace period stay quiet). STILL OPEN: (a) the Quick Entry and Settings utility windows render no status row, so a person capturing through Quick Entry while offline still gets no indication; (b) apps/web has no equivalent surface at all; (c) the row deliberately is NOT a live region, because the workspace contract pins exactly one announcer (test/e2e/accessibility.spec.ts:112) -- whether an offline transition SHOULD be announced, and by which single announcer, is an unmade product decision.

open_items.item: Fixed deadlines in the macOS lane are tuned standalone but consumed in `--all`, which runs about 1.6x slower
open_items.detail: Measured by 03-19 on application_digest=e1c9d695da26507ae3a6a3b711f6884df5602022efe62d4a0b0cdf5b389754a4. A6's final case ('after discarding changes and navigating away') failed inside a full --all run with 'last read was nothing', while the SAME row passed 4/4 standalone. Row duration: 39.5s inside --all against 24.9-25.5s standalone. The preceding VoiceOver-layer rows leave an AX client attached and every focus change costs more under one. The specific race was a deadline asymmetry INSIDE A6 -- it waited 10s for a dialog to OPEN but only 5s for focus to be restored after one CLOSES, even though restoration is the slower operation (the destructive branch commits a route change, re-renders the list, and runs two focus effects). Fixed by making both 10s, which weakens nothing: usableFocus(last) is asserted exactly as before and settledFocus still returns whatever it last saw at the deadline, so genuinely lost focus still fails loudly. GENERALISE: every other fixed timeoutMs/sleep in tooling/verify-macos-integration.mjs was chosen against standalone timings and is therefore under-budgeted in the context the gate actually runs it in. Audit them against --all timings rather than waiting for each to flake once. This does not invalidate O-29's bound; it names a mechanism the bound covers.
open_items.closed_detail: Closed by 03-20 by removing per-row deadline tuning entirely rather than auditing each deadline against --all timings. tooling/verify-macos-integration.mjs now defines ONE lane-wide WAIT_SCALE that multiplies every bounded wait (waitFor, settledFocus, ensureFrontmost, the launch and teardown loops), applied UNIFORMLY rather than only under --all -- a mode-dependent factor would recreate the very standalone/--all split the item describes. Scaling weakens no assertion and costs nothing on the happy path: a wait whose condition is already true returns on its first poll, so the larger budget is spent only on a genuine failure. The generalisation clause is also satisfied: 31 non-polling sleep() calls were converted to wait on the observable consequence of the preceding action, leaving 9 sleeps, all inside polling loops or Promise.race deadlines, none preceding an action. MEASURED after the change on application_digest=937b279ce76952f0180c31ca1cf0deee0ccd42b199a13116d5f22adcfe3c2684: A3 took 11554-11924ms inside five consecutive --all runs against 11752-11894ms standalone -- the asymmetry the item names (29.5s vs 14.6-16.5s) is gone, not merely padded. Five consecutive --all runs at rows=15 failed=0 cases=92; gate lanes=9 failed=0.

open_items.item: NO desktop test at any level contacts a real Keepling server -- blocks MAC-03, MAC-05 and SRV-02's Electron adapter proof
open_items.detail:
BROADENED 2026-09-04. Filed originally as 'packaged tests use the stub'. The truth is larger and was found by verifying a citation instead of trusting it. apps/desktop/test/e2e/real-stack-sync.spec.ts, DESPITE ITS NAME, constructs KeeplingSyncAdapter with a stubbed `fetch` against the non-resolving host https://server.keepling.invalid (lines 35-36, 327-328, 497-498). Every spec in test/packaged/ sets KEEPLING_TEST_SYNC_MODE and so exercises the inline stub SyncPort. The only desktop test touching localhost is gap-closure.spec.ts, which stands up a bare 500-responding loopback server and a closed port to prove offline DETECTION -- not synchronization. So the Electron adapter has NEVER exchanged a byte with Phoenix.

Consequences: MAC-03's 'later reconcile' clause, MAC-05's 'not only a development renderer ... synchronizes' clause, and SRV-02's Electron adapter proof all rest on a fake. This is O-20's rule applied to the largest remaining subsystem: code that has only ever executed under fixtures is not proven code.

FEASIBLE, and cheaper than it looks: apps/web/e2e/support/stack.ts already spawns real PostgreSQL and Phoenix for the web lane, and the packaged specs already spread ...process.env so they can be pointed at a base URL. The work is wiring the desktop lane to that existing harness, not building a server story from scratch.

NOTE ON MY OWN ERROR: MAC-03 was checked on 2026-09-04 citing this spec as real-server proof, and unchecked hours later once the citation was actually read. A test named 'real-stack' that stubs its transport is exactly the kind of thing this ledger exists to catch, and the name did the deceiving.

PARTIALLY ADVANCED 2026-09-04 by 03-21, then BLOCKED on O-37. The shared harness half is done and committed (772ea1a): the real PostgreSQL + migrations + seed + Phoenix half of apps/web/e2e/support/stack.ts was EXTRACTED to apps/web/e2e/support/backend.ts and is now imported by stack.ts, so a desktop lane can reuse the exact harness the web lane proves against instead of a second drifting copy. The environment caveat recorded elsewhere in this handoff does NOT apply here: PostgreSQL 18.6 starts cleanly on this machine, there is no shmget failure, and the refactored stack was observed reaching 'Keepling Playwright stack ready at http://127.0.0.1:4173' with real Phoenix.

The lane itself is blocked, and by something larger than tooling. Probed directly against that running real server with a real device grant obtained through the real /oauth/authorize -> code -> PKCE /oauth/token path (token 200, five-field server-derived namespace origin=http://localhost:4002 issuer=http://localhost:4002 server_instance=local-test generation=1 account_subject=00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001): GET /api/v1/sync returns 200 for the device bearer, but POST /api/v1/commands/capture-task and GET /api/v1/mutations/{id} both return 401 authentication_required for the SAME bearer. See O-37. Until that is decided, the packaged app can authorize and pull against real Phoenix but structurally cannot push, so the must_have 'reaches Synced only on an exact receipt' is unreachable against a real server and no honest lane can assert it.

open_items.item: CLOSED - Quick Entry focus restoration and window-level Escape binding
open_items.detail:
MEASURED directly on application_digest=937b279ce76952f0180c31ca1cf0deee0ccd42b199a13116d5f22adcfe3c2684 with a standalone AXProbe diagnostic, twice, deterministically. Sequence: open Quick Entry by the real global accelerator, type a draft, tab to "Discard Draft...", Space, then Space on "Keep Draft". Observed focus after the dialog closes: AXWebArea "Keepling" -- the DOCUMENT, not the "Discard Draft..." button that opened the dialog. apps/desktop/renderer/quick-entry.tsx binds its Escape handler with onKeyDown on a div INSIDE the React root, so a keydown targeted at the document never reaches it: Escape was posted and BOTH windows were still present 2s later (windows=["Keepling","Keepling - Inbox"], capture fields=2). Tabbing back into the capture field first and posting the SAME Escape hid the window immediately (windows=["Keepling - Inbox"], capture fields=1). So a person who opens the discard confirmation and keeps their draft loses Escape as a way out of Quick Entry until they tab somewhere. WHY A6 DOES NOT CATCH IT: usableFocus() accepts any non-AXApplication node with a non-zero frame, and the AXWebArea qualifies -- focus is 'usable' but is not on the invoking control, which is what WAI-ARIA requires of a dismissed dialog. Tightening usableFocus to exclude AXWebArea/AXGroup container roles would turn this into a red row; that is a deliberate decision for a later plan, not a silent change. 03-20 did NOT work around it silently: A3 and A6 use Escape there only as teardown and now call returnFocusIntoQuickEntry() first, with the finding named in the helper's comment. Compare Keep Editing in the workspace unsaved-changes dialog, which restores focus correctly -- so this is specific to the Quick Entry alertdialog, and the fix is a ref-based restore in quick-entry.tsx.

CLOSED 2026-09-04 by 03-21 (302f13e), with BOTH defects fixed rather than only the visible one. (1) The discard confirmation now returns focus to the control that OPENED it when that control still exists (Keep Draft), and to the title field when it does not (Discard Draft unmounts 'Discard Draft...' along with the draft, so the fallback is the live path on the confirm branch, not decoration). (2) Escape and Command-Return moved from '<div onKeyDown>' to a WINDOW-level keydown listener, held through a ref so it registers once and still sees the current draft and submission state. That makes the guarantee structural: there is no focus position inside the Quick Entry window from which Escape can fail, so the next dialog that returns focus to nowhere cannot re-arm this trap. Deliberately NOT a main-process global accelerator -- Escape is a window-local key and a global one would swallow Escape from every other application on this Mac. RED first: both new @windowed tests in test/e2e/keyboard-quick-entry.spec.ts failed before the change (the second timed out with the window still open, which is the defect verbatim); 7/7 pass after, with no existing assertion weakened. macOS rows A3 5/5 and A6 6/6 PASS. usableFocus() in tooling/verify-macos-integration.mjs still ACCEPTS the AXWebArea and is deliberately left alone -- tightening it is a real follow-up (it is what made A6 blind here) but would turn unrelated rows red, so it is carried as its own decision and not smuggled into this fix.

open_items.item: The Mac app's device grant cannot issue a mutation or read a receipt -- the server has no such route, so "Synced" is structurally unreachable against real Phoenix. NEEDS A DECISION.
open_items.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-04 by 03-21 while building the O-34 real-stack lane, by doing exactly what O-34 asked: pointing a real client at a real server. It is a product defect, not a test problem, and it was invisible for as long as every desktop test faked its transport.

MEASURED against real Phoenix (MIX_ENV=test) on real PostgreSQL 18.6, using a device grant obtained through the REAL browser-delegated path (POST /api/v1/test/session for the browser half, then GET /oauth/authorize -> 302 keepling://auth/callback?code&state -> POST /oauth/token with the PKCE verifier -> 200 with the five server-derived namespace fields):
  GET  /api/v1/sync                     -> 200  (device bearer accepted)
  POST /api/v1/commands/capture-task    -> 401 authentication_required
  GET  /api/v1/mutations/{mutation_id}  -> 401 authentication_required
Same bearer, same connection, same second.

CAUSE, in the router: the :device_grant_authenticated pipeline (KeeplingWeb.Auth#authenticate_device_grant) covers only /api/v1/device-grants*, /api/v1/sync and /api/v1/sync/bootstrap. Every /api/v1/commands/* route and GET /api/v1/mutations/:id sit behind [:api, :authenticated, :mutation], which requires a BROWSER SESSION COOKIE and, through :mutation -> require_trusted_origin, an Origin header matching the request host. KeeplingSyncAdapter sends a Bearer token and no cookie and no Origin, by design. The published contract agrees with the server, not with the client: packages/contracts/openapi/keepling.yaml declares the DeviceBearer security scheme on /device-grants* and /sync* only, and declares no security at all on /commands/* or /mutations/{id}.

CONSEQUENCE: the shipped Mac app can authorize, bind its namespace, and pull, but it can never push. DesktopApplication.runSyncPass throws on the first push, settles retryable_failure, and the outbox correctly keeps the exact serialized bytes forever. Nothing is lost and nothing lies -- 'Saved on this Mac' stays truthful -- but 'Synced' is unreachable against a real server, and MAC-03 / MAC-05 / SRV-02's Electron adapter proof cannot be honestly completed until this is resolved.

WHY THIS STOPPED RATHER THAN BEING AUTO-FIXED (deviation Rule 4): the fix decides WHICH CREDENTIAL CLASS MAY MUTATE DATA. It changes a published contract with its own gate (contracts:check), it changes the server's authentication surface for the entire command API, it requires deciding whether require_trusted_origin -- a browser CSRF defence -- applies to a non-browser client or must be replaced by something else for it, and it requires new authorization plumbing to derive the account context the command controllers read (conn.assigns.current_account_id) from a device grant, which today assigns only current_device_grant_id and device_grant_namespace. None of those files are in 03-21's scope, and REQUIREMENTS.md deliberately phases SRV-02 across adapters, so 'which adapters may mutate' is a live design question rather than an oversight to paper over.

OPTIONS FOR THE DECIDER (not ranked -- this is the decision):
  A. Extend the device-grant pipeline to the command surface and the mutation lookup, update the OpenAPI security declarations to match, derive account context from the grant, and state explicitly what replaces require_trusted_origin for a bearer client.
  B. Add a distinct native command surface (e.g. /api/v1/native/commands/*) so the browser surface's CSRF posture is untouched, and point KeeplingSyncAdapter at it.
  C. Accept it for this milestone: record that the Mac app is pull-only against a real server, land the real-stack lane asserting exactly that (authorize + pull real, push refused, never Synced, exact bytes retained), and move the push proof to the phase that owns it.
Option C is the only one that needs no server change, and it is honest, but it means MAC-03/MAC-05 stay unchecked with a stated reason rather than becoming checkable in Phase 3.
